# Project plan

**Title:** LabFlow: independent core delivery and gated enterprise integration

**Summary:** Build the approved single-server Web application with relational persistence and background jobs. Deliver Stage A without external systems, then complete mandatory Stage B through mock development, protected activation and real sandbox evidence. The implementation plan is in English; the product interface remains Simplified Chinese.

**Workload unit:** relative work units

**Parallel capacity:** 3

Workload is approximate. T+N denotes a relative position, not hours, working days, or elapsed calendar duration. Task bar length represents workload; full-row hatching indicates a blocked state only.

The schedule uses input task order as its stable priority and releases dependencies when predecessor work finishes. This deterministic list schedule does not guarantee a global optimum.

## Assumptions

- This is a new independent English plan authored directly from demo/labflow/requirements.md v1.1; the original Chinese requirements remain unchanged. English was explicitly requested for planning artifacts.
- The fixed plan review cap is 2 full revision-and-review cycles after the mandatory initial independent review. Review status is determined by the separate review record, never by this input.
- Task FIXTURE is the simple relative-work reference of 1. Other ordinary estimates of 2 or 3 are rough ratios including implementation or authored design, tests, documentation and expected review corrections. T+N denotes an abstract sequence position, not hours, days or calendar time; business deadlines and recovery targets do not convert to project duration.
- Capacity is at most 3 ordinary tasks. The four exact resource locks are available at T+0 and held throughout each listed task; the formal shared environment still requires ENV delivery. Milestones and external nodes consume no capacity.
- Dependencies release only after accepted, merged delivery with usable contracts. Resource conflicts do not create business dependency edges. Positive-work design tasks include review and revision; separate zero-work freeze gates approve their outputs.
- Asset sandbox, documents, test token and sample assets are assumed ready at the abstract position T+6, as expressly promised by the fictional client. This is a planning scenario and no real delivery-date guarantee.
- Real OIDC metadata, registered callback, client credentials and all three sandbox-account classes have unknown readiness. IDENTITY_READY has external_ready:null. Its exact descendants remain unscheduled; core and mock work and real assets have no dependency on it.
- Approved architecture remains a browser frontend, /api/v1/ server, relational database and background-job process. Reviewed design chooses the concrete repository/runtime, database mechanisms, UI, OIDC checks, sync cursors and migration strategy without new service layers or speculative scope.
- All implementation PRs include their own local unit/contract/transaction tests. Formal QA PRs modify test harnesses, fixtures and reports only; a failure requiring server, adapter or persistence changes returns to the owning implementation PR with backend-lead and, when its data model/integrity/migration changes, db-reviewer before revalidation.
- Partial prerequisite implementations may merge behind disabled routes/capabilities until their dependent business closure arrives; they cannot advertise an incomplete rule as a usable finished capability. Frontend tasks use frozen-contract mocks; real wiring waits for the corresponding accepted backend.
- Integration code, simulators and migration preparation may be developed before A. Application external-integration flags remain off until A_RELEASE; B_ACTIVATE additionally waits for restored binding-data and compatible upgrade/rollback proof. Simulators run only in detached development/test contexts before that gate.
- Local/isolated-test containers are the delivery environments; no production infrastructure or ongoing duty staffing is added. Test and demo databases are separate and use the exact synthetic source fixtures with independent clock/data resets for every scenario.

## Risks

- Unknown real identity readiness prevents the real OIDC branch, its cross-integration acceptance and B/full release; no estimated internal task substitutes for the provider materials.
- Transaction races, deadline-first convergence and outbox recipient snapshots are central correctness risks; adversarial tests must protect terminal states and partial-rollback behavior.
- Identity mode switches and the last emergency administrator guard can lock out recovery if evaluated outside one transaction; no simulator or initialization recovery may bypass them.
- Asset cursor failure, source-time ties and first binding can corrupt existing identity/creation-time relationships if recovery is implemented as destructive rescan; backup and restore proof precede real use.
- The deterministic input-order schedule is reproducible but not globally optimal. Unscheduled B work still has rough workload estimates; the latest scheduled position is not the project completion date.
- Any failed or missing explicit acceptance condition blocks its phase. Business/technical representatives must sign actual evidence, including fixed performance samples and real-provider account classes; implementers cannot waive it.

## Task details

### FIXTURE · Specify synthetic fixtures and independent reset protocol

Preserve the source laboratory/user/device identities, qualification dates and clock baseline in a fixture manifest. Separate baseline, temporary-password, initialization, report and integration branches.

- **Deliverable:** Reviewed fixture manifest and reset/clock specification.
- **Acceptance criteria:** LAB-A/LAB-B, USR-01..06, DEV-01..03, fixed names/codes/roles, 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z device creation and 2026-11-02T00:00:00Z initial clock are recorded faithfully., USR-07/08 are additional isolated fixtures only; baseline passwords are already set and baseline USR-05 qualifies for local emergency use., Each of source section 5 scenarios 1..32 has a reset/clock branch and planned evidence destination; synthetic tests and demos have distinct databases.
- **PR scope:** One small documentation PR for the fixture manifest and repeatable reset protocol.
- **Requirements:** REQ-035, REQ-036
- **Estimate basis:** A small static fixture/reset specification establishes the reference workload of 1. Includes the scoped implementation/design or test execution, supporting tests, documentation, review and expected corrections.
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Resource locks:** None

### D_DATA · Design relational entities and transactional integrity

Choose the minimal relational design and transaction strategy for stable entities, revisions, effective half-open occupancy, credential/session state, immutable audit, deduplication and outbox. Specify deadline convergence as a system operation after authentication/scope checks and before manual rules.

- **Deliverable:** Reviewed schema, migration outline, transaction/race tables and invariants.
- **Acceptance criteria:** All minimum fields/relationships in source section 3, immutable IDs/laboratories/creation time and 409 version conflict behavior are mapped., Define atomic conflict protection for same-device reservations/maintenance, last organization administrator, grant uniqueness, successful idempotency keys and business/audit/outbox commits., Convergence preserves terminal states, survives failed manual transactions, cannot authorize out-of-scope effects, and makes read/list/availability/report results logically current., Architecture remains one server plus jobs and relational storage; review resolves necessary corrections before freeze.
- **PR scope:** One design PR for core persistence and transactional integrity; no platform-wide implementation.
- **Requirements:** REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-009, REQ-010, REQ-011, REQ-012, REQ-013, REQ-014, REQ-015, REQ-016, REQ-017, REQ-018, REQ-019, REQ-020, REQ-021, REQ-022, REQ-023, REQ-024, REQ-033, REQ-034, REQ-035
- **Estimate basis:** About 3 reference workloads for cross-entity schema, occupancy transactions, audit/outbox invariants and race review. Includes the scoped implementation/design or test execution, supporting tests, documentation, review and expected corrections.
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Resource locks:** backend-lead, db-reviewer

### D_API · Design authorization, API and list contracts

Specify /api/v1/ endpoints, permitted role unions, scope/error matrix, password/session states, stable list contracts and safe summaries. Select a concrete repository/runtime without adding unapproved architecture.

- **Deliverable:** Reviewed route, field, error, pagination and authentication contract with mock examples.
- **Acceptance criteria:** 401 unauthenticated, 404 foreign/sensitive out-of-scope records, 409 business/version conflicts and 422 located validation errors carry stable code/message/request correlation., Default 20/max 100 pagination, business-time descending plus immutable ID ordering, 100-character search and inclusive-local-date/exclusive-next-day conversion up to 90 days are explicit., No public signup, self-reset, batch approve/cancel/role-edit, new-laboratory entry, secrets in responses or name-based identity matching is introduced., Temporary-password lifetime, ordinary/local/enterprise separation and next-request permission changes are specified for every protected endpoint., Freeze qualification grant/revoke/read endpoints and their scoped administrator versus owner-read-only matrix, including validity inputs, current/history responses, duplicate grant conflicts, no direct validity edit and retained revocation consequences. Define authorized name editing of the two fixed laboratories within the reviewed administrator role/scope matrix; lab IDs, administrator scopes and historical device relations do not change, and no laboratory-create or device-lab-migration endpoint is added.
- **PR scope:** One core API/authentication contract PR with examples and reviewed scope matrix.
- **Requirements:** REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-007, REQ-017, REQ-020, REQ-021, REQ-022, REQ-023, REQ-024, REQ-031, REQ-035, REQ-013
- **Estimate basis:** About 2 reference workloads for a bounded endpoint/error/scope catalog and pagination/authentication examples. Includes the scoped implementation/design or test execution, supporting tests, documentation, review and expected corrections.
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Resource locks:** backend-lead

### D_STATE · Design reservation and maintenance state operations

Write exact operation/state/precondition tables and transaction boundaries for reservation timing, qualifications, effective maintenance, emergency isolation and work orders.

- **Deliverable:** Reviewed state-transition and adversarial-operation specification.
- **Acceptance criteria:** UTC ISO 8601 inputs, Asia/Shanghai displays, 08:00-20:00 including weekends, half-hour grid, 30-minute..8-hour same-day reservations and inclusive now+30-minute/start&lt;=now+30*24-hour limits are explicit; end may exceed the start horizon., Pending expiry=min(created+24h,start), approved no_show=start+15m and in_use completion=end precede applicable manual rules, including failed reschedules and management operations., Owner cancellation differs from pre-start-only manager cancellation/rescheduling; registration uses \[start,start+15m); automatic end is statistical/system-inferred, not hardware control., Maintenance may span days/closed hours; cancellation preserves original intervals and releases only remaining occupancy. Work-order transitions, eligibility, no closed editing and unresolved-emergency re-enable barrier are fixed.
- **PR scope:** One state/invariant design PR with race tables and boundary examples.
- **Requirements:** REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-009, REQ-010, REQ-011, REQ-012, REQ-013, REQ-014, REQ-015, REQ-016, REQ-022, REQ-035
- **Estimate basis:** About 3 reference workloads because deadline priority and concurrent reservation/maintenance state matrices require adversarial review. Includes the scoped implementation/design or test execution, supporting tests, documentation, review and expected corrections.
- **Dependencies:** D_DATA
- **Resource locks:** backend-lead

### D_NOTIFY · Review complete event and reminder delivery matrix

Define every listed business event, non-sensitive message summary, event-time recipients, delivery authorization and reminder/compensation state. No recipient rule is delegated to unreviewed implementation choices.

- **Deliverable:** Reviewed notification matrix and delivery/retry protocol.
- **Acceptance criteria:** Creation, approval, rejection, reschedule, cancellation, expiry, start, end, no_show, affected qualification revocation, fault and isolation events all have explicit recipients and summaries., Event-time enabled lab_manager/org_admin scope union is frozen, applicant result and actual-user isolation recipients are included, role-union duplicates removed; deactivation/revocation retaining in_use notifies scoped managers., Delivery skips disabled/lost-scope recipients without adding newly privileged users; skip differs from delivery failure; unique event/recipient/type is enforced., Start reminder requires unchanged slot, approved state and now&lt;start on automated/restart/manual paths; 1/5/15-minute retries allow exactly three retries and failed events remain actionable.
- **PR scope:** One event/recipient/reminder contract PR including semantic review and examples.
- **Requirements:** REQ-002, REQ-008, REQ-009, REQ-010, REQ-011, REQ-012, REQ-013, REQ-015, REQ-018, REQ-019, REQ-020, REQ-024, REQ-031
- **Estimate basis:** About 2 reference workloads for the complete event/recipient matrix and one coherent retry/reminder protocol. Includes the scoped implementation/design or test execution, supporting tests, documentation, review and expected corrections.
- **Dependencies:** D_API, D_STATE
- **Resource locks:** backend-lead

### D_UI · Design Chinese pages, interactions and accessibility

Specify the required Chinese page set, frozen-contract mocks, responsive forms/lists and dialog/keyboard behavior. User data stays plain text and protocol identifiers stay unchanged.

- **Deliverable:** Reviewed UI flows and component/page state specification.
- **Acceptance criteria:** Directory/details/day view, reservation/self-list/use registration, work orders, messages, workbench, reports, audit, account and integration administration are accounted for., Loading, empty, field failure, permission refusal, version conflict, network failure and success states are specified at 360px and 1440px., Keyboard flow, associated labels/errors, focus-visible and non-color cues, dialog focus entry/return/Escape/close and deliberate approve/cancel confirmation are explicit; availability has an equivalent text list., Device administration explicitly includes scoped qualification grant/revoke controls with validity intervals, current/history display, deliberate revoke confirmation, conflict/permission feedback and no direct validity edit. Owners have read-only access to their own qualifications. Include authorized name-edit controls for the two existing labs, preserving fixed IDs and providing no lab-add or device-migration control.
- **PR scope:** One UI specification PR with mock fixtures and review corrections.
- **Requirements:** REQ-004, REQ-017, REQ-020, REQ-021, REQ-025, REQ-026, REQ-036, REQ-013
- **Estimate basis:** About 2 reference workloads for reviewed page/component state designs, using the already defined API/state contracts. Includes the scoped implementation/design or test execution, supporting tests, documentation, review and expected corrections.
- **Dependencies:** D_API, D_STATE, D_NOTIFY
- **Resource locks:** frontend-lead

### D_OPS · Design local/test deployment and safe data operations

Choose container/repository deployment, migrations and compatible rollback strategy, initialization authority, protected configuration/credential references, backup retention and restore procedure for the approved environment scope.

- **Deliverable:** Reviewed deployment/migration/backup design and upgrade compatibility matrix.
- **Acceptance criteria:** Default external flags off; core liveness/database-write readiness and separate external degradation are defined., Ordinary initialization is idempotent; explicit authorized expired-initial-admin reset preserves ID/audit and does not bypass enterprise emergency guards., Daily data/config backup, protected separate credentials, latest seven copies, failure detection and blank-isolated recovery proof are specified with &lt;=24-hour loss and &lt;=60-minute target., Upgrade requires verified backup and compatible schema/application versions; destructive migration is explicitly handled rather than assuming application rollback restores data. Logs retain 30 days while history/audit/messages are not auto-deleted.
- **PR scope:** One deployment and data-operations design PR with reviewed migration/rollback plan.
- **Requirements:** REQ-002, REQ-024, REQ-031, REQ-033, REQ-034, REQ-036
- **Estimate basis:** About 2 reference workloads for one local/test deployment and migration/backup compatibility specification. Includes the scoped implementation/design or test execution, supporting tests, documentation, review and expected corrections.
